title: Finding the service gaps behind tenant satisfaction
summary: I benchmarked Platform Housing’s tenant satisfaction, tested unusual year-on-year changes and examined complaint findings to recommend where customer-service teams should focus next.
scenario_note: The datasets, calculations and workbook are real. The workplace brief, stakeholder roles and proposed follow-up actions are simulated to explain how I would use this analysis in a housing association. I did not work for Platform Housing.
brief: Ahead of an annual board review, the Director of Customer Experience needs a clear account of tenant satisfaction: how Platform compares with similar landlords, where services fall behind and which changes need investigation before the report goes to the board.
requirements_intro: I structured the brief around the decision, comparison group, measures and evidence needed. For this portfolio scenario, the resulting scope is an annual benchmark and a prioritised investigation plan; it is not an evaluation of individual tenants or a costed service redesign.
requirements_summary: An overall satisfaction score can conceal service weaknesses, while changes in recording can distort the annual performance report.
How does Platform compare with similar landlords? Which services warrant attention? Are large changes comparable across years? Do escalated complaints support the same priorities?
Give the board a defensible account of performance and help customer-experience, repairs and neighbourhood teams choose the next investigations.

Published 2023/24 and 2024/25 Tenant Satisfaction Measures, plus a separate comparison of Housing Ombudsman reports labelled 2025/26. No tenant-level records, intervention costs or implemented outcomes.

requirements_template.intro: This is the framework I would use in a stakeholder discussion. The applications below distinguish analytical choices made here from decisions requiring an actual business owner.

items.prompt: Who will use the report, and which decision should it support?
items.application: A Director of Customer Experience briefs the board and agrees investigation priorities with Repairs and Neighbourhoods. These stakeholder interactions are simulated.

items.prompt: Which periods, housing stock and landlords form a relevant comparison?
items.application: Use low-cost rental survey measures and a primary cohort of 17 housing associations with more than 40,000 homes, including Platform. Keep the separate 21-landlord Ombudsman sample and its reporting period explicit.

items.prompt: Which measures answer the brief, and how should differences be explained?
items.application: Report satisfaction percentages, differences from the peer median and year-on-year movements. Distinguish survey perceptions, operational target compliance and Ombudsman findings. Associations guide investigation; they do not predict a satisfaction increase.

items.prompt: Which internal records would explain the published aggregates, and how would access be controlled?
items.application: Request de-identified survey responses, repair-job histories and complaint records through the relevant data owners. Confirm permissions, minimum fields, retention and secure handling before linking records. None were available here.

items.prompt: Are denominators, targets and coding rules comparable, and do extracted totals reconcile?
items.application: The workbook exposes large changes in repairs and case counts. Reconcile inclusion rules and source totals with service owners. Resolve the Ombudsman rate/count discrepancy and small peer-category extraction differences before formal reporting.

items.prompt: Which deliverables, review dates and checks would make the report ready for use?
items.application: An Excel benchmark, a concise board report and an investigation log are the proposed outputs. Agree the deadline, owners and acceptance criteria; require unresolved data issues to be corrected or explicitly qualified.

items.prompt: Which existing targets apply, and how would an intervention be assessed?
items.application: The published repair comparison uses a 28-day target in both years. Confirm its coverage before treating it as comparable. Agree service measures, resources and review dates for any pilot; no new target or benefit estimate is assumed.

data_requests: Compare service experiences and investigate differences across tenant groups.
Published landlord-level TSM returns only; no respondent-level data.
Reconcile repair counts, completion dates and the 28-day target.
Published rates and counts recorded in the workbook; no job histories.
Review themes, escalation and response times.
Published TSM aggregates and Ombudsman reports; no internal case files.
Select a relevant peer cohort and calculate benchmark medians.
Public Regulator of Social Housing returns and 21 Ombudsman reports.
data_intro: Inside a housing association, I would normally request these records from their owners and agree definitions before joining them. Here, I used public regulatory returns and report extracts. The evidence supports landlord-level comparisons, but cannot explain an individual tenant’s experience.
priorities_intro: I combined the size of Platform’s gaps with the way service scores move together across landlords. The strongest association with overall satisfaction concerns well-maintained homes. Listening and communication also combine meaningful shortfalls with strong associations, making them sensible starting points for a service review.
priorities: Review how tenant feedback reaches service teams and how actions are reported back.
Review repair updates, expected completion dates and explanations when plans change.
Investigate repeat repairs and unresolved maintenance issues alongside tenant feedback.
actions: Reconcile the repair population and completion measure before attributing the annual change to service performance.
A documented bridge between years, agreed definitions and an explained residual change.
Test clearer updates and feedback follow-through with a defined tenant group.
Compare survey feedback, repeat contacts and unresolved issues before and after the pilot; agree targets first.
Investigate communal-area satisfaction by estate and review cleaning and inspection records.
A local issue list linked to inspection evidence, accountable owners and review dates.
Review repairs-related findings and reconcile the Ombudsman extraction against the original reports.
An agreed findings total, explained rate denominator and a verified set of recurring service themes.
